# 2 Samuel Chapter 3 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 170v–172r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_003_page_001.jpg, 2SA_003_page_002.jpg, 2SA_003_page_003.jpg

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** The war between the house of Saul and the house of David was long. David grew steadily stronger, while the house of Saul grew steadily weaker.

**2** Sons were born to David in Hebron: his firstborn was Amnon, by Ahinoam of Jezreel; **3** his second, Chileab, by Abigail the widow of Nabal the Carmelite; the third, Absalom the son of Maacah, daughter of Talmai king of Geshur; **4** the fourth, Adonijah the son of Haggith; the fifth, Shephatiah the son of Abital; **5** and the sixth, Ithream, by Eglah, David's wife. These were born to David in Hebron.

**6** During the war between the house of Saul and the house of David, Abner was strengthening his own position in the house of Saul.

**7** Now Saul had a concubine whose name was Rizpah the daughter of Aiah. And Ish-bosheth said to Abner, "Why have you gone in to my father's concubine?"

**8** Abner became very angry at the words of Ish-bosheth and said, "Am I a dog's head — of Judah? To this day I show covenant-faithfulness to the house of Saul your father, to his brothers and to his friends, and I have not delivered you into the hand of David — and now you charge me with a fault concerning this woman?

**9** May God do so to Abner and more also, if I do not accomplish for David what the LORD has sworn to him — **10** to transfer the kingdom from the house of Saul and to establish the throne of David over Israel and over Judah, from Dan to Beersheba."

**11** And Ish-bosheth could not answer Abner another word, because he feared him.

**12** Then Abner sent messengers to David on his behalf, saying, "To whom does the land belong? Make your covenant with me, and my hand shall be with you to bring all Israel over to you."

**13** David said, "Good. I will make a covenant with you. But one thing I require of you: you shall not see my face unless you first bring Michal the daughter of Saul when you come to see my face."

**14** Then David sent messengers to Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, saying, "Give me back my wife Michal, whom I betrothed to myself for a hundred foreskins of the Philistines."

**15** And Ish-bosheth sent and took her from her husband, from Paltiel the son of Laish. **16** Her husband went with her, weeping as he went, all the way to Bahurim. Then Abner said to him, "Go, return." And he returned.

**17** Now Abner had been conferring with the elders of Israel, saying, "For some time you have been seeking David as king over you. **18** Now act — for the LORD has spoken concerning David: 'By the hand of my servant David I will save my people Israel from the hand of the Philistines and from the hand of all their enemies.'"

**19** Abner also spoke privately to the Benjaminites. Then he went to Hebron to report to David all that Israel and the whole house of Benjamin were prepared to support.

**20** When Abner came to David at Hebron with twenty men, David made a feast for Abner and the men who were with him.

**21** Abner said to David, "Let me arise and go, and I will gather all Israel to my lord the king, that they may make a covenant with you, and you may reign over all that your heart desires." So David sent Abner away, and he went in peace.

**22** Just then the servants of David and Joab returned from a raid, bringing great plunder with them. Abner was no longer with David in Hebron, for he had sent him away, and he had gone in peace.

**23** When Joab and all his army arrived, he was told, "Abner the son of Ner came to the king, and the king sent him away, and he went in peace."

**24** Joab went to the king and said, "What have you done? Abner came to you — why did you let him go? He has gotten clean away!

**25** You know Abner the son of Ner — he came to deceive you, to learn your movements, and to find out everything you are doing."

**26** Joab left David and sent messengers after Abner, and they brought him back from the cistern of Sirah. But David did not know it.

**27** When Abner returned to Hebron, Joab drew him aside into the gateway as though to speak with him privately. And there he struck him in the belly, and he died — for the blood of Asahel his brother.

**28** When David heard of it afterward, he said, "I and my kingdom are forever innocent before the LORD of the blood of Abner the son of Ner.

**29** May it fall upon the head of Joab and upon all his father's house! May the house of Joab never be without one who has a discharge, or who is a leper, or who holds the spindle, or who falls by the sword, or who lacks bread!"

**30** So Joab and his brother Abishai killed Abner, because he had killed their brother Asahel at the battle of Gibeon.

**31** Then David said to Joab and to all the people with him, "Tear your garments, put on sackcloth, and mourn before Abner." And King David walked behind the bier.

**32** They buried Abner in Hebron. The king lifted up his voice and wept at the grave of Abner, and all the people wept.

**33** The king lamented over Abner:
"Should Abner die as a fool dies?

**34** Your hands were not bound,
your feet were not placed in chains.
As one falls before sons of wickedness, you fell."
And all the people wept over him again.

**35** All the people came urging David to eat while it was still day, but David swore, "May God do so to me and more also, if I taste bread or anything else before the sun goes down!"

**36** All the people took notice of it, and it pleased them — as everything the king did pleased all the people.

**37** So all the people and all Israel understood that day that it had not been the king's will to put Abner the son of Ner to death.

**38** The king said to his servants, "Do you not know that a prince and a great man has fallen this day in Israel?

**39** I am weak this day, though anointed king; these men, the sons of Zeruiah, are too hard for me. May the LORD repay the evildoer according to his wickedness."

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

All three translators agree on the structure: David's sons in Hebron (vv.2-5), Abner's break with Ish-bosheth (vv.6-11), Abner's covenant with David and the Michal exchange (vv.12-21), Joab's murder of Abner (vv.22-27), and David's public mourning and self-exoneration (vv.28-39). The chapter's central theme — the intersection of political pragmatism and personal vengeance — is consistently recognized.

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.1 — "long" vs. "dragged on"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "the war...was long"
- **PNEUMA:** "the war...dragged on"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "was long" — more neutral; "dragged on" implies tedium not in the Hebrew *arukkah*.

### V.6 — "making himself strong" vs. "strengthening his position" vs. "consolidating his own power"
- **EMET:** "making-himself-strong"
- **LOGOS:** "strengthening his position"
- **PNEUMA:** "consolidating his own power"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "strengthening his own position" — LOGOS's wording with "own" added from PNEUMA to capture the reflexive *mitchazzeq*.

### V.7 — "gone in to" vs. "slept with"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "gone in to my father's concubine"
- **PNEUMA:** "slept with my father's concubine"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "gone in to" — the Hebrew *ba el* is the standard biblical euphemism; "slept with" is a modern equivalent that loses the register.

### V.8 — "burned to Abner" vs. "became very angry" vs. "exploded with rage"
- **EMET:** "it-burned to-Avner exceedingly"
- **LOGOS:** "Abner became very angry"
- **PNEUMA:** "Abner exploded with rage"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "became very angry" — LOGOS balances accuracy with readability. PNEUMA's "exploded" over-dramatizes *charah me'od*.

### V.12 — "on his behalf" / "immediately" / "in his place"
- **EMET:** "in-his-place"
- **LOGOS:** "on his behalf"
- **PNEUMA:** "immediately"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "on his behalf" — the Hebrew *tachtav* here means "on his own behalf" or "in his stead," not "immediately."

### V.14 — "won for the price of" vs. "betrothed for"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "betrothed to myself for a hundred foreskins"
- **PNEUMA:** "won for the price of a hundred foreskins"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "betrothed to myself for" — the Hebrew *erastiy* is "I betrothed," the formal marriage term. PNEUMA's "won" is too transactional.

### V.24 — "going away" vs. "he is gone" vs. "walk out"
- **EMET:** "he-went, going away [halokh halakh]"
- **LOGOS:** "so that he is gone"
- **PNEUMA:** "you just let him walk out"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "He has gotten clean away!" — captures Joab's indignation at the infinitive absolute *halokh halakh* (emphatic departure).

### V.29 — "holds the spindle" vs. "is crippled"
- **EMET:** "one-who-holds the-spindle [pelek]"
- **LOGOS:** "one who holds the spindle"
- **PNEUMA:** "who is crippled"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "who holds the spindle" — the Hebrew *machaziq ba-pelek* is debated (distaff vs. crutch), but the literal rendering preserves the ambiguity. PNEUMA's "crippled" is one interpretation.

### V.33 — "fool" vs. "senseless fool"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "as a fool dies"
- **PNEUMA:** "like some senseless fool"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "as a fool dies" — *naval* already carries the sense of senselessness; "senseless fool" is redundant.

### V.39 — "tender" vs. "weak" vs. "powerless"
- **EMET:** "tender and-anointed king"
- **LOGOS:** "weak, though anointed king"
- **PNEUMA:** "I may be the anointed king, but today I am powerless"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "weak this day, though anointed king" — *rakh* means "soft/tender/weak." LOGOS captures the paradox concisely. PNEUMA's "powerless" overstates it.

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
